title: Scroll timeline fallback and no-JS visibility
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

Landing page reveals each section with `animation: reveal linear both; animation-timeline: view();` on `.section`, where the keyframes start at `opacity: 0`. The base stylesheet also sets `.section { opacity: 0 }` and a script adds `.is-visible` from an IntersectionObserver. QA on Firefox and with JavaScript disabled reports blank sections. Review and repair.

checks.reason: The fix must guard the scroll timeline behind an @supports feature query.
Content must stay visible when JavaScript is unavailable.
The answer must address the engine without scroll timelines.
Scroll-driven animations are not Baseline; claiming universal support is an anti-pattern.

rubric: The base state is visible content; hidden starting states are applied only inside @supports (animation-timeline: view()) or after script confirms support.
